Paragon Aquatics is an American manufacturer of pool deck equipment, based in LaGrangeville, New
York. It makes stainless steel starting platforms, diving towers, water polo goals, lifeguard
chairs, ladders and rails for commercial and institutional pools. The company traded as Paragon
Swimming Pool Co. in the 1960s and as KDI Paragon from about 1970 into the late 1990s, and has
been part of [Pentair](pentair.md) since 1999.[^sw6608][^sw7005][^ai2005] In competitive swimming
its platforms supply the base of the [Colorado Block](../equipment/swimming/starting-blocks/colorado-block.md),
built with [Colorado Time Systems](colorado-time-systems.md).[^pca103]

## History

This section follows the company through its changes of name and owner.

### Paragon Swimming Pool Co.

In 1966 the company advertised in Swimming World as Paragon Swimming Pool Co., Inc., of
Pleasantville, New York. One of those advertisements introduced a stainless steel competitive
starting platform with a removable backstroke bar that fitted a single deck socket, and placed it
in the company's ParaFlyte deck equipment line. The same advertisement claimed ten years of
leadership.[^sw6608] Counting back from 1966 gives a start in about 1956. Pentair's
2015 catalog says instead that the company has been in business for more than 60 years, which
would put the start a little earlier.[^pca103] No primary founding record has been found.

### KDI Paragon

By May 1970 the company's advertisements carried the name KDI Paragon Inc., after its owner
[KDI](kdi-corporation.md), and the company was still in Pleasantville.[^sw7005] No source found dates KDI's purchase of the company. A company history
of Sylvan Pools describes KDI as a Cincinnati conglomerate with interests in swimming pools,
defense electronics and plastics, which bought a controlling stake in Sylvan in 1969.[^fu-as]
Aquatics International, however, places KDI, which it calls Paragon's holding company, in
LaGrangeville in 1989.[^ai2008] The sources do not explain the difference. A 1986 advertisement
describes Paragon as "a KDI company".[^st8608]

Under KDI the company promoted itself to the people who design pools. In 1972 it held a one-day
pool design conference in New York for architects and builders, at which the coaches James
Counsilman and Fred Kahms spoke; the company's president, Leonard Berens, said it was called
because a small number of architects designed most American pools.[^sw7201] A fourth national pool
design seminar followed in San Francisco in 1977.[^sw7708]

KDI itself was taken private in a leveraged buyout in 1988 and sold off many of its businesses
from 1989 onward.[^fu-as] Tom Saldarelli became Paragon's president in 1991.[^ai2005]

### General Aquatics, Essef and Pentair

Aquatics International reports that Paragon was sold to [General Aquatics](general-aquatics.md) in 1995 and passed to
[Essef](essef.md), the owner of the pool equipment maker Pac-Fab, in 1997.[^ai2005] Essef acquired General
Aquatics in May 1997.[^fu-as] Pentair completed its purchase of Essef on 10 August 1999, for about
$310 million.[^pentair8k] By then the company was listed as Paragon Aquatics, with a telephone
number in the LaGrangeville area rather than Pleasantville.[^st9904] Advertisements in 2002
described it as a division of Pentair Pool Products.[^st0207]

Saldarelli stayed through each sale and stepped down in 2008, after nearly two decades with the
company. By then the parent was Pentair Water Pool and Spa of Sanford, North Carolina.[^ai2008]
Pentair still sells the starting platforms under the Paragon name, and its 2015 catalog gives the
address as 1351 Route 55, LaGrangeville.[^pca103][^pentair]

### Paragon Awards

The 2015 catalog states that Paragon presents the annual Paragon Awards with the International
Swimming Hall of Fame. Awards are made for swimming and diving in competition, for water polo
and synchronized swimming, and for recreation and aquatic safety.[^pca103]

## Products

This section covers the company's competition equipment in detail and its other lines briefly.

### Starting platforms

Paragon's platforms share one construction: a welded stainless steel pedestal, polished and
passivated, carrying a top made from a single sheet of polypropylene 1-1/4 in thick. The top
has a grooved, sand-finished non-skid surface, which the company describes as
patented.[^pca103] The polypropylene top replaced earlier designs in about 1991, when Paragon
advertised sixteen platform models and a new grooved top.[^st9102] The tops come in two sizes:
the standard top, 24 × 20 in, and the larger track start top, 24 × 32 in, which suits the
track-style start.[^pca103]

The 2015 catalog sorts the range by height, top size and number of legs:

- Full-height single-leg platforms with a standard top, in Classic, Shortee, Florida and Long
  Reach versions for different pool edges. The Florida model sits on a raised curb beside the
  gutter, and the Long Reach sets the anchor further back for deck-level pools whose overflow
  gutter is broad.
- Full-height platforms with a track start top: the single-leg Track Start Quickset and the
  dual-leg [Track Start Competitor](../equipment/swimming/starting-blocks/track-start-competitor.md)
  in side-step and Long Reach rear-mount versions.
- The dual-leg Competitor with a standard top, in Classic and Long Reach versions.
- The low-height [Varsity](../equipment/swimming/starting-blocks/paragon-varsity.md) series.[^pca103]

Some of these models date from the 1980s. A Long Reach version of the single-post Paraflyte
platform, set further back from the wall for rimflow and deck-level pools, appeared in
1982.[^st8202] The [Quickset](../equipment/swimming/starting-blocks/paragon-quickset.md) platform,
which drops into a covered deck socket and lifts out without tools, was advertised as new in
1986, and Paragon called it the first platform of that kind.[^st8608] In 1989 the company
redesigned its whole line on the Quickset principle, as the two-leg Competitor and four
single-post styles: Shortee, Standard, Long Reach and Florida.[^sw8907] The Varsity models followed
in 1990 for a revised high-school rule that limited some platforms to 18 in above the
water.[^st9008]

The [Track Start PLUS+](../equipment/swimming/starting-blocks/track-start-plus.md) kits add an
adjustable backplate and side hand grips to track start platforms. The STS version brings a
sliding backplate to standard-size tops.[^pca103] Tops can be ordered in Pantone colors with
custom logos, and the company refinishes older tops with the current groove pattern.[^pca103]

### Anchors

Three anchor families hold the platforms in the deck. The Paraflyte anchor is cast bronze, and
the platform bolts to it, so tools are needed to fit or remove it. The Quickset anchor (single
leg) and the Competitor anchor (dual leg, 6 in or 10 in deep depending on the setback) are
Dual-Wedge designs. In these a tapered base locks the bottom of the post, and a wedge tightened
by a hand knob locks the top, so the platform comes out without tools. With the platform off the
deck, the wedge parts sit in the socket and a cover closes it.[^pca103]

The tapered base is the subject of US Patent 5,660,013, filed in 1996 by Saldarelli, Jerry Amato
and William Duffelmeyer and assigned to KDI Paragon.[^taperlock] Paragon advertised a Taper-Lock
conversion kit for existing Quickset anchors in 1997.[^st9710] Basketball hoops in the catalog
mount in the same anchors.[^pca103]

### Diving equipment

Paragon makes 1 m and 3 m diving towers in three lines. The Paraflyte towers come with the ladder
at the rear or at the side; the side-ladder version takes three feet less deck. Each comes in
Ultraflyte, Superflyte and Topflyte grades, which differ only in tube wall thickness. The Duradapt
tower takes a Durafirm fulcrum and is intended for competition pools with 16 ft boards. The
Sportflyte is a recreational tower that the catalog says is not for competition. A stair-entry
system can be fitted to new or existing 3 m towers.[^pca103]

The Duradapt was introduced in 1980 as a factory-built tower designed around the Durafirm
fulcrum.[^st8005] Paragon advertised a geared adjustable fulcrum for its Paraflyte towers in
1975.[^sw7503] The 2015 catalog lists Duraflex, Maxiflex B, Paraflex and Century boards. It notes
that the governing bodies accept only a 16 ft board, 20 in wide with a 24 in fulcrum range, for
competitive diving.[^pca103]

### Other competition equipment

Paragon water polo goals are built to the NCAA, NFHS, USA Water Polo and FINA rules. The posts are
118 in apart on the inside, and the cage height is adjustable. The legs fold flat for storage on
deck, and the goals stand in deck sockets shared with stanchions.[^pca103] A redesigned goal with
folding legs and a choice of net or solid backing, for the USS and NCAA rules respectively, was
announced in 1992.[^st9205]

The catalog also lists anti-turbulence racing lanes in 25 yd, 25 m and 50 m lengths, lane storage
reels, finish and backstroke pennant lines, stanchions for recall and pennant lines, and
underwater observation windows.[^pca103] Paragon advertised the windows for coaching and
filming swimmers and divers in 1989.[^sw8912]

### Other products

The rest of the range is recreational and safety equipment: fixed, moveable and portable
lifeguard chairs, including the Griff's Guard Station series; pool ladders, grab rails and
steps; and underwater lights and speakers.[^pca103]

## In swim timing

The [Colorado Block](../equipment/swimming/starting-blocks/colorado-block.md), launched in 2002,
pairs a Paragon track start platform with Colorado Time Systems relay judging equipment. Paragon
supplies the platform, a stainless steel sponsor panel, and brackets for the start horn and
[deck plate](../equipment/swimming/deck-cabling/cts-quickconnect-deck-plate.md).[^sw0204][^pca103]
The panel slides open for access and comes off without tools. The adapter kits are sold for the
Track Start side-step, Long Reach Track Start rear-mount, Standard Competitor, Long Reach
Competitor and standard Paraflyte or Quickset platforms.[^pca103] The block's design patent is
assigned jointly to Colorado Time Systems and Paragon Aquatics.[^d471945]

## In competition

KDI Paragon advertised in 1975 that its Paraflyte platform had been the only one used at the 1974
AAU national senior championships in Concord, California.[^sw7505] Through the 1970s and 1980s,
meet announcements in Swimming World listed "Paragon blocks" among a host pool's features, beside
the lane lines and timing system.[^sw7610] Pentair's catalog says the platforms are in wide use at
FINA, NCAA, NFHS, US Masters Swimming and USA Swimming events, and shows them at the 2011 Pan
American Games in Guadalajara.[^pca103]
